fields.h1: Build a Recruiting Intake Form for Every Open Role
fields.hero_description: Build a recruiting intake form that gets the must-haves, salary range, and interview panel from hiring managers up front.
fields.features_heading: What the Hiring Manager Answers Once
fields.features_subheading: Describe your roles and who approves them. Emergent builds the form, the routing, and the table your recruiters work from.
fields.feature_1:
Must-haves kept apart from nice-to-haves

Ask the hiring manager for no more than three must-haves, then list the rest as nice-to-haves. Recruiters screen against the short list and use the long one to break a tie.
fields.feature_2:
Salary range and level, asked up front

The form asks for the level, the salary range and whether the role is remote, hybrid, or on site. Each answer is required, so a recruiter knows the budget before the first call.
fields.feature_3:
The interview loop, named before sourcing

List every interview stage, who sits on it and how long it runs. Candidates hear the whole process on the first call, and each panelist knows their slot a week ahead.
fields.feature_4:
Each role routed to its recruiter

Send engineering roles to one recruiter and sales roles to another, by email or in Slack. A role above the salary limit you set waits for an approver before anyone is assigned.
fields.feature_5:
Every intake saved as a record you own

Each submitted intake becomes a record in a database you own, with its team, level, location, and date. Filter open roles by any of them, or list the ones still missing answers.
fields.feature_6:
The full codebase, exported to GitHub

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository when intakes need to sit next to an applicant tracking system you already run. Host it anywhere and keep building.

fields.usecase_heading: From the Hiring Manager to the First Search
fields.tab_content_1:
Edric has all 3 must-haves before the call

Bellgrove Search sends each new client an intake link before the kickoff call. At Tilsley Foods, plant manager Zofia Szymanska fills it in for a night shift maintenance supervisor. She names 3 must-haves, a salary range of $82,000 to $94,000, and a 2-stage interview. Recruiter Edric Lowther gets the whole intake by email.
fields.tab_content_2:
All roles over $160,000 wait on the VP

Kestrian Robotics caps what a hiring manager can open alone. A senior firmware engineer request comes in with a salary top of $185,000. Any role with a top over $160,000 waits for Pernille Aspelund, the VP of People, who gets a Slack message to approve it. Once she approves, the app assigns a recruiter.
fields.tab_content_3:
On one intake, 40 pickers in 2 shifts

Peak season at Haverell Freight means hiring in bulk. Site manager Arvo Ellory files one intake for 40 seasonal pickers, with 24 on the night shift and 16 on days, and gives each shift its own start time. The app turns it into 2 requests, one per shift, and the recruiters filling nights work a separate list from the day team.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every open intake on one table, 2 past 3 days

Folarin Okonkwo-Lind runs recruiting at Calloran Software, where 14 intakes are open. Each row shows the role, the team, and the missing answers. An intake unanswered for more than 3 days emails its hiring manager a reminder. This week 2 reminders went out, and the oldest, for a data engineer, has waited 5 days.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Recruiting Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a recruiting intake form that gets every answer from the hiring manager before sourcing starts.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Limit the must-have field to three
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask for the money and the level
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the questions your recruiters ask in every intake meeting: title, team, manager, location, and start date. Those become the required fields. Anything a recruiter asks only for some roles goes in an optional section lower on the form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give must-haves a field that takes three entries and nice-to-haves a separate box. The limit forces the hard choice before sourcing starts, when changing a requirement costs nothing, and not after the first round of interviews.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Make the level and the salary range required, along with any bonus or equity. Recruiters need the budget before the first candidate call, and a range the hiring manager typed in settles later debates about what was agreed.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Have the hiring manager list each interview stage, who runs it, and how long it lasts, plus the week panelists are free to start. Recruiters can then book panel time before the first strong candidate is ready to move.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Set the rules that route each intake: which recruiter takes which team, and which roles need sign-off first, such as any salary top over a limit you pick. Send each approval to the approver in Slack or by email.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Set a reminder for missing answers
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick how long an unanswered intake can wait before its hiring manager gets a reminder, such as 3 days. Show recruiters which answers are still missing, so the kickoff call is spent on those and nothing else.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Build it and run one live role
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe the intake questions, approvals, and reminders to Emergent in plain English, and it builds them with a database you own. Run one open role through it, read what came back, and change any question by prompting.

plan.angle: The pages ranking for this term are question lists and downloadable templates for the intake meeting between a recruiter and a hiring manager. None shows what happens after the hiring manager answers. This page shows a working form across four real setups: an agency taking a new client role, an in-house team where high-salary roles need sign-off, a warehouse asking for seasonal headcount by shift, and a recruiting lead watching which intakes are still unanswered. Every intake is saved to a database the team owns.
